proposal.description: The blanking history cp_delay only advances in S_RUN and forgets S_SS, so through soft start it holds the zero left by the idle clear and every soft-start sample reads as not faulted.
proposal.reason: In S_SS, if cp_sync stays high over trip_ss switching cycles, fault_count_ss_out stays 0 and window_trip_SS never asserts. In the original design both rise.

proposal.description: The S_RUN shift register stores the live cp_sync at pwm_rise, while the run count adds the blanked cp_delay sample, so the bit later subtracted as leaving is not the bit that was added.
proposal.reason: In S_RUN, take a cycle where the comparator was low BLANK_CLKS clocks before turn-on but is high at pwm_rise. WINDOW_RUN cycles later that cycle's bit leaves the window and is subtracted although it was never added, so fault_count_run_out wraps below zero and window_trip asserts falsely. The opposite case leaves counts stuck in the window.

proposal.description: The soft-start shift register stores the live cp_sync at pwm_rise, while fault_count_ss adds the blanked cp_delay sample, so the bit later subtracted as leaving is not the bit that was added.
proposal.reason: In S_SS, take a cycle where the blanked sample is clear and cp_sync is high at pwm_rise (or the reverse). When that cycle's bit leaves the 32-cycle window, fault_count_ss_out is decremented for a fault it never counted (or keeps a fault forever), so the count drifts and window_trip_SS asserts wrongly or too late.

after: always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
proposal.description: The soft-start telemetry output is registered, so fault_count_ss_out shows fault_count_ss one clock late instead of the live count.
proposal.reason: On the clock after a pwm_rise in S_SS that changes the count, fault_count_ss_out still shows the old value. On the clock after the idle clear it still shows the pre-hiccup count instead of 0.
